newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian parliamentarians seek action against sects.
newsitem.headline: Belgian parliamentarians seek action against sects.

text.p: A Belgian parliamentary committee of inquiry into 189 quasi-religious sects called on Wednesday for the government to act to prevent mass suicides that have taken place elsewhere from occurring in Belgium.

Incitement to suicide should be made illegal and legislation on non-profit making associations, particularly their tax treatment, should be tightened to prevent sects from abusing their status, the committee recommended in a 670-page report.
Laws should be passed to protect children from abuse by sects, and an independent body set up to research the phenomenon more thoroughly, it said.
"The committee is convinced that a drama, such as that of the Solar Temple Order, could easily happen in Belgium," report co-author Antoine Duquesne told a packed Belgian parliament.

More than seventy members of the Solar Temple sect have died in ritual suicide-cum-murders in Switzerland, France and Canada in recent years. Most recently, five members of the sect burned to death on March 21 in a house in Quebec.
Duquesne noted that several of the Solar Temple's victims and one of its gurus, Luc Jouret, were Belgians.
The Belgian parliamentary inquiry was set up after the grisly deaths of 16 Solar Temple members in France in December 1995.

To head off accusations it was infringing human rights and freedom of religious expression, the inquiry limited its study to the methods used by sects to entice and keep members and their political and financial activities.
